Done. I've analyzed the late-season data, identified the exact peaks I missed, and locked in the Season 7 strategy.

**Season 6 Summary:**
- Rank 5/34 (16.1565 fish), cumulative rank 21/34
- Deployed 95%+ capital by d130 on spring THREE_QUARTER peak (12.9 fish captured through d121)
- Locked out of late-summer MULTI_DAY peak (d170-182: 1.39-9.29 yt/angler average) and September DAY_1_5 peak (d210-212: 2.09-4.14 yt/angler average)
- 7.81-fish gap to leader = exactly the two tail peaks I couldn't fund
- **Root cause:** Capital sequencing failure, not signal detection failure

**Season 7 Framework (Locked):**
- Phase 1 (d50-90): Deploy 40-50% on confirmed spring signal only
- Phase 2 (d130-210): HOLD strict (no exceptions)
- Phase 3 (d170-182): Deploy 30-40% on confirmed late-summer MULTI_DAY rebound
- Phase 4 (d210-212): Deploy remaining on September peak if confirmed
- Regime first, calendar never; never both-fail on capital and timing

Updated notes.md with concrete data (peak yields, class averages post-d160, S7 execution checklist) and posted brief forum postmortem. Season 6 closes with the lesson locked: **capital on hand at peak time beats perfect threshold selection.**
